register.name: Extended Credit Facility
register.detail: IMF · Approved 12 January 2024 · fifth review 6 July 2026 · access raised to SDR 87.08 million (140% of quota) · extended to 11 July 2027
register.note: Approved at about $100 million in January 2024; SDR 55.97 million (about US$75.98 million) disbursed to date
register.text: The IMF’s main lending programme with The Gambia, supporting reforms to address long-standing structural impediments to inclusive growth. In July 2026 the Board extended it by six months and added SDR 12.44 million, 20% of quota.

register.name: Resilience and Sustainability Facility
register.detail: IMF · Approved June 2025 · 18 months, access of 75% of quota · second review 6 July 2026 · extended six months
register.note: SDR 10.36 million (about US$14.06 million) released on the second review
register.text: Supports climate resilience reforms alongside the Extended Credit Facility. The second review, in July 2026, released SDR 10.36 million.

register.name: Regional Access Increase and Sustainable Energy Project (RAISE)
register.detail: World Bank Group (IDA) · Approved 24 June 2026 · with ECOWAS · West Africa Regional Electricity Market Program
register.note: $160 million for Togo and The Gambia together; the share of The Gambia is not stated
register.text: Expands and densifies electricity distribution networks, lowers the cost of connection and speeds up renewable energy in Togo and The Gambia, with about 1 million people to be connected across the two. It serves energy, the standard furthest from reach.

register.name: The Gambia Infrastructure Project
register.detail: World Bank (IDA) · Approved 29 May 2025 · 60 km of roads · 80 rural communities connected to the grid
register.text: Builds 60 kilometres of climate-resilient rural and urban roads and connects 80 rural communities to the electricity grid, with about 142 km of medium-voltage and 350 km of low-voltage lines. A credit enhancement mechanism is to unlock $60 million of private investment in renewable energy; it serves energy and livelihood.

register.name: Trade Finance Facility for strategic commodities
register.detail: BADEA · Signed in Riyadh, 2 September 2026 · BADEA’s second trade finance facility to the Government
register.note: Signed by the President of BADEA and the Minister of Finance and Economic Affairs
register.text: Finances the import of strategic commodities for food security and other national priorities. It serves the food standard, where 47.2% of Gambians are moderately or severely food insecure.

register.name: Gambia Renewable Energy
register.detail: EIB · Five signatures, 27 December 2018 to 31 July 2026 · promoter NAWEC · total cost about €149 million
register.text: Grid-connected solar power with battery storage, grid reinforcement to cut losses and take up more renewable power, and off-grid solar and battery units for rural health clinics, secondary schools and food facilities. It serves energy, the standard furthest from reach.

register.name: Cattle Production and Productivity Improvement Project
register.detail: IsDB · Signed 19 June 2026, at the IsDB Group Annual Meetings in Baku
register.note: Signed by the Minister of Finance and Economic Affairs
register.text: A financing agreement to raise cattle production and productivity. It serves the food and livelihood standards.

register.name: University of The Gambia, Phase II
register.detail: BADEA · Amendment Number One signed 26 December 2025 · furniture and equipment
register.note: Signed during the first official visit of BADEA’s President to The Gambia
register.text: Amends a USD 16 million BADEA loan for the second phase of the University of The Gambia, covering the supply of furniture and equipment. It serves the education standard.

register.name: Sustainable Water Supply, Greater Banjul
register.detail: EIB · Approved 10 December 2025 · signed 23 December 2025 · promoter NAWEC · total cost about €59 million
register.note: Two signatures of €22.1 million and €8 million, the latter an investment grant
register.text: Finances the infrastructure for safely managed drinking water in the Greater Banjul Area, keeping service for about 560,000 people and reaching about 300,000 new beneficiaries. It serves the water standard, where 48.2% have safely managed drinking water.

register.name: Resilience Building, Vulnerable Youth and Women Support Project
register.detail: African Development Bank Group · Approved by the Board · grant, Transition Support Facility (prevention envelope) · Basse, Kuntaur and Janjanbureh
register.note: 1,500 new direct jobs; 500 women-led small businesses and 50 women’s cooperatives
register.text: A grant to tackle fragility in Basse, Kuntaur and Janjanbureh: skills for young people, credit for women-led businesses, climate-smart farming, four rehabilitated primary health facilities and nutrition surveillance for 22,000 children. It serves food, health and livelihood.

register.name: School of Medicine and Allied Health Sciences, University of The Gambia
register.detail: IsDB · Approved at the 361st meeting of the Board of Executive Directors · release of 7 July 2025
register.note: To train doctors, nurses and public health experts in The Gambia
register.text: Helps establish a school of medicine and allied health sciences at the University of The Gambia, to address the shortage of health professionals. It serves the health and education standards.

register.name: Salam Financial Services, loan for small businesses
register.detail: IFC · Approved 21 November 2025 · signed 29 June 2026 · three years, in Gambian dalasi · MSME Finance Platform
register.note: IFC’s share of a loan of up to $2 million; up to $1.2 million from parallel lenders
register.text: A senior loan to the second largest microfinance institution in The Gambia, for on-lending to micro, small and medium enterprises and low-income households, half of it for women-owned or women-led businesses. It serves the livelihood standard.

register.name: Climate Resilient Fishery Initiative for Livelihood Improvement (PROREFISH Gambia)
register.detail: GCF FP188 · Approved 20 July 2022 · FAO · 30% disbursed · completion estimated 28 October 2028
register.text: Climate-proofs artisanal fisheries and their infrastructure, improves fish processing and diversifies local food systems for fishing communities. It serves the food and livelihood standards.

register.name: Large-scale Ecosystem-based Adaptation in The Gambia
register.detail: GCF FP011 · Approved 30 June 2016 · UNEP · grant, 100% disbursed · completion estimated 8 January 2026
register.text: Restores at least 10,000 hectares of degraded forests, mangroves, savannahs and farmland, and supports community-run natural resource enterprises. It serves the food and livelihood standards, and the forest on this page.

items.name: The Farmland
items.label: Of the land in agriculture, 2024
items.text: Three quarters of the land in agriculture, along the river and its floodplain.

items.name: The Forest
items.label: Of the land under forest, 2024
items.text: Standing forest that stores carbon and water, and can earn as it stands.

items.name: The Fresh Water
items.label: Renewable fresh water a person, 2022
items.text: Rain and rivers renewed every year: power, irrigation and drinking water.

items.name: The River
items.label: Gambians along one river, 2025
items.text: A whole nation built along one river and its Atlantic mouth: water, fish and a port to price as assets.

items.name: The People
items.label: Citizens, 2025
items.text: 39.7% are under fifteen: the workforce and the market of the next generation.

items.name: Salam Financial Services
items.text: The second largest microfinance institution in The Gambia, with 15 branches, lending to small businesses and low-income households. IFC signed a loan in June 2026, half of it for women-owned or women-led businesses.
